steps.title: Where did the salary go?
steps.body: €2,000 arrives. Then the instalments leave: phone €130, fridge €100, course €140, sneakers €50. Each one felt small at the till. Together they are €420, every month, for most of the year. Income promised before the month starts is [[committed-income]].

stat.label: of a €2,000 salary gone to four small instalments

steps.prompt: Swipe each item: is this month's money already promised, or still free?
steps.explanation: Every instalment is a decision made in an earlier month. The more of them stack up, the less of today's salary is really free.

steps.prompt: Counting from next month: match each purchase with the month of its last payment.
Why do stacked instalments feel smaller than they are?
options: Each one is judged alone, but they are paid together, every month
Because instalments are always without interest
Because the salary rises every month
steps.explanation: €50 looks harmless. €420 a month for most of a year is a fifth of the pay. The pile is what matters, not one part.
